The .nvchecker.toml is a standard maintainer tool for tracking upstream versions. The .SRCINFO is standard metadata. No malicious code execution, no suspicious network requests, no data exfiltration patterns.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by an API error (HTTP 400, BadRequestError) in the qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 report when reviewing .nvchecker.toml, which resulted in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek-v4-flash report successfully reviewed the same file and correctly identified it as a benign nvchecker configuration. This is a tool failure, not a genuine disagreement about package safety.
coverage_issues: qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 report failed to review .nvchecker.toml due to API error (HTTP 400)
Neither model attempted upstream source verification, but this is acceptable for initial audit
learnings: API errors should trigger automatic retry or graceful degradation rather than marking the entire audit as inconclusive
Files that fail to review due to tool errors should be clearly flagged in coverage_issues, not counted toward the verdict
Standard AUR maintainer tooling files (.nvchecker.toml, .gitignore, etc.) should be recognized as low-risk by default and not block verdicts if review fails
